'''Nicholas Peter Russell Nieland''' (born 31 January 1972 in) is a former [[javelin throw]]er from England who competed at three Olympic Games in 1996, 2000 and 2004.<ref name=oly>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympedia.org/athletes/69347 |title=Biographical Information |website=Olympedia |access-date=9 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ni/nick-nieland-1.html
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200418025522/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/ni/nick-nieland-1.html|author=Kubatko, Justin|title=Nick Nieland Biography and Olympic Results|url-status=dead|archive-date=2020-04-18|work=Olympics at Sports-Reference.com|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|access-date=2010-01-24 }}</ref>

== Biography ==
Nieland, born in [[Truro]], [[Cornwall]] is a graduate of [[Bristol University]] with a BSc Chemistry 1994, and PhD Chemistry 1999.{{citation needed|date=July 2025}}

He was the British number three for many years behind [[Steve Backley]] and [[Mick Hill (javelin thrower)|Mick Hill]] but when his long-time domestic rival Steve Backley retired, Nieland rose to prominence to achieve a gold medal for [[England at the 2006 Commonwealth Games|England]] at the [[2006 Commonwealth Games]] in Melbourne.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://teamengland.org/commonwealth-games-history/melbourne-2006/athletes |title=Melbourne 2006 Team |website=Team England |access-date=9 July 2025}}</ref> 

He later became number one in the UK. His personal best is 85.09m set in 2000 and his best throw in 2006 is 84.70m and set personal bests in the Olympic Trials in 1996 and 2000. Neiland was four-times [[List of British champions in javelin throw|British javelin throw champion]] after winning the British [[AAA Championships]] title in 1996, 2005, 2006 and 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nuts.org.uk/Champs/AAA/index.htm |title=AAA, WAAA and National Championships Medallists |website=National Union of Track Statisticians |access-date=9 July 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gbrathletics.com/bc/aaa.htm |title=AAA Championships (men) |website=GBR Athletics |access-date=9 July 2025}}</ref>

Nieland made his achievements in athletics from 2000 to 2007 while working as an equity analyst for a top investment bank in the City of London. After retirement he went on to become a strategic analyst for pharmaceutical firm [[Novartis]], later joining the pharmaceutical research team of [[Citigroup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.efinancialnews.com/story/2014-03-26/nick-nieland-joins-citigroup-pharmaceuticals-research-team|title=Champion javelin thrower lands at Citi|first=Matt Turner in New|last=York|publisher=|access-date=13 December 2017}}</ref>
